app.notes:
Setup: Node 24.11.1 pinned in mise.toml (the repo's .nvmrc says 24 and engines says >=24). Run .ui-capture/build.sh, which does: npm ci, then the repo's own `npm run build` (tsc + vite build), copies dist/ to .ui-capture/out, adds the seed loader, then runs the seed generator and .ui-capture/seed/finalize.mjs. The seed generator (.ui-capture/seed/generate.seed.tsx with data in seed/data.ts) runs under the app's own vitest/jsdom setup and replays about six months of use through the app's own code: AppProvider and FileSystemProvider (the same addUser/addUserToGroup/setOnboardingComplete calls Onboarding.tsx makes), plus createDirectory/createFile/moveToTrash, MailService and MessagesService. It moves the clock with vi.setSystemTime, so files, mails and messages have real dates between 2026-05-22 (install) and 2026-11-17. finalize.mjs maps asset URLs to the hashed files in the production build.

What the entry URL shows: the game always opens on a 'CLICK TO START' splash, followed by the main menu, a boot log and the login screen. On its own that leaves the page nearly blank (only the start button). out/aurora-autopilot.js, loaded right after the seed loader, therefore performs the returning player's own steps through the real UI: click Initialize System, skip the logo, choose Continue (enabled because a save exists), wait for the boot log, then pick Mira Calloway and log in with her password from the users DB. After about 6–8 s the page is the logged-in desktop (Aurora wallpaper, fuchsia accent, WiFi 'Calloway-5G'), with the saved window session restored: a Finder window and the Mail app open on the seeded inbox. Add ?intro (e.g. /?intro) to turn the autopilot off and click through by hand: Continue, then Mira Calloway, password nightowl42 (hint: 'bird that stays up late'; root password: admin).

Data: player Mira Calloway, an InfoSec student at Aurora University who takes freelance pentest jobs. About 60 files under /home/mira: Documents/{Notes, University course folders, Freelance client folders with scopes/findings/invoices, CTF writeups, Finance csv}, Projects/{portscan-lite, dotfiles, wifi-survey}, Desktop scratch files, Downloads, Pictures (4 photos plus a screenshot), Music (2 tracks), one item in Trash, and .bash_history. Mail (TrustMail account mira.calloway@trustmail.com / Tr0ub4dor&3; the app logs in automatically via ~/.Config/mail.json): 53 emails covering client threads, a professor, the registrar, family, sent replies and newsletters (TechBlog, HackWithJack, SecureBank, Aurora University), mixing read/unread, starred, archived and trashed, with one attachment. Messages (logs in automatically as 'mira'): 84 messages with 7 contacts (devon, sasha, nana, jack_hwj, rosa.hollowpine, priya, theo_ta), several unread, 2 starred. Calendar: about 120 events from June to December 2026, including recurring classes in a custom 'University' category, client work, CTFs, social, family and deadlines (e.g. the Hollow Pine on-site visit on Nov 20 and a proposal due Nov 24). Installed via the App Store (FileSystemProvider.installApp): Notepad, Messages, Calendar, Music, Photos. The Dock shows Finder/Browser/Mail plus Terminal/Settings; the others are in the Dock's overflow (grid) menu, which is how the app lays out more than 3 user apps. Also seeded: a saved window session (Finder + Mail), Notepad with 3 open tabs (one with unsaved edits), Browser history and bookmarks, the notification center, terminal input history, and known WiFi networks.

Main areas: Desktop and Dock, the Finder file manager, Terminal, Browser (in-game sites such as aurora.edu, techblog.com, hackwithjack.org, securebank.com and trustmail.com), Mail, Messages, Calendar, Notepad, Photos, Music, Settings, DevCenter and the App Store. Clearing site data, or choosing 'New Game' and then reloading with sys_seed_applied removed, brings the seed back. Verification: Chrome cannot start inside this sandbox, so .ui-capture/seed/smoke.check.tsx renders the real <App/> in jsdom at 1440x900 with out/seed.json loaded, runs the shipped out/aurora-autopilot.js and checks the stages: intro, then the menu (~1.5 s), the login screen (~6 s) and the desktop (~6.4 s), where the seeded Desktop files, the Finder window and the Mail inbox are visible. Run it with: npx vitest run --config .ui-capture/seed/vitest.seed.config.ts smoke.

# Running it
- Follow the repo's own setup docs and tooling. Take the simplest route that shows the real app: a static production build if the front end works without a backend, otherwise the app's own server (production or dev mode).
- If it needs a database or other services, run them locally with an embedded or file-based option (SQLite, in-memory, JSON files, an embedded Postgres such as PGlite) or the app's demo/mock mode.
- Don't redesign or restyle anything. Change only what's needed to build and run it.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):
- Give the required variables placeholder values so the app starts.
- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). Docker isn't available. A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4466 (e.g. 5466) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4466 is stopped before I check.

# When you're done, leave this in ./.ui-capture/
- app.json: {"mode": "static" or "server", "entry": "/path where the main UI opens", "login": null or {"username": "...", "email": "...", "password": "..."}, "stubs": [{"service": "what was faked", "how": "how"}], "notes": "how you set it up, what data is loaded, and the main areas of the app"}
- static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4466/ (it gets PORT=4466). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

# Order of work
You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
1. Get the app building and running with its stubs, and write the contract above (app.json plus out/ or start.sh), even if it has only a little data so far.
2. Then build out the data, re-running your seed and checking the app still loads after each substantial step, so that a working state with the data loaded so far is always in place.
Write large data sets with a short generator script rather than as one long literal file.
